day.text: I've said it: as Falcon I visited Ellis and learned they visited Alex. Casey, you just repeated that exact result, so your Falcon story is copied from mine. Only one of us is Falcon, and that's me.
day.note: I already said what my Falcon learned. Casey is now repeating my exact result, which fits a copied story. I'll point that out and state that I'm the Falcon.

day.text: Blair's Eagle story holds: visiting Casey with Alex as a visitor gives you +1. The open issue is Casey and Drew both claiming Falcon. Casey, Drew: did your Falcon visit to Ellis show Ellis's visitor and destination, and who else visited Ellis?
day.note: Blair's Eagle story now holds together: visiting Casey, who had Alex as a visitor, gives Blair +1. The Falcon conflict between Casey and Drew is still open, so I'll ask for specifics and hold my throw.

day.text: I'm throwing at Casey. My Kookaburra read said Hawk, and Casey now says Falcon, the same claim Drew made.
day.note: Casey is the leader and my Kookaburra read on Casey conflicts with Casey's current Falcon claim. I'll throw S2, a low card, at Casey.

day.text: Casey and Drew, your Falcon results are identical, so one of you is copying. I'm Eagle, I'll throw at whichever of you can't say where Ellis went. Ellis, where did you go last night?
day.note: I'm Farm Eagle. Casey and Drew give identical Falcon results, so one is copying. I'll commit to throwing at whichever one can't give Ellis's destination during the vote.

day.text: I'm throwing at Casey. Casey copied my Falcon result, and I'm the only Falcon.
day.note: Casey is falsely claiming the Falcon I hold and copied my result. Alex is also throwing at Casey. I'll cast one vote with the Wild W6, which costs nothing if Farm wins.

day.text: Ellis: I visited Alex last night with the Hawk, and I can't see my visitors, so I can't confirm anyone visited me. Casey and Drew, your Falcon results match word for word, so I'm throwing at Casey.
day.note: I answer Blair's question honestly: I visited Alex. Casey and Drew both claim the same Falcon result, so I lean toward Casey, the leader, as the copy, and I'll throw at Casey with a low card.

day.text: I'm throwing at Casey. Casey and Drew gave identical Falcon results, and only one can be the Falcon.
day.note: Most of the table is throwing at Casey over the duplicate Falcon result, and Casey is also the score leader. I'll join the Casey vote.

day.text: Casey: Ellis, you can't confirm who visited you, so your Hawk story is all we have. I'm throwing at you because your vote for Casey doesn't come with any proof of where Drew's Falcon result came from.
day.note: I'm the Meowfia Sphinx, and Ellis's Hawk claim is true, so Ellis is Farm. Throwing at Ellis helps my side if Ellis is executed, and it adds a vote against the table's pile-on.

Alex.note: As Farm Kookaburra I'll visit Casey to learn their role and check Casey's Eagle claim, since that story was contested.

Blair.note: I'm Farm Eagle with no information yet. I'll visit Casey, who has been making claims about visitors, to learn who came to them and gain eggs for each visitor.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia as the Sphinx. Farm roles in play are Eagle, Falcon, Hawk, Kookaburra, and Tit. I'll pick Hawk and visit whoever holds it to learn their identity.

Drew.note: I'm Falcon, Farm. Ellis is the leader on points, so I'll visit Ellis to learn who they visited.

Ellis.note: As Hawk I gain an egg only if my visited player is Meowfia. Alex's claims shifted between rounds, so I visit Alex to test that.

Finley.note: As Tit I visit one player and guess a role. Pigeon is the most common Farm animal, so I'll guess it on Drew, who is mid-table and unexplored.

audit: Blair lays 1 egg in Blair's nest

Alex.feeling: Tense and confusing: two players claim Falcon, my own confused Kookaburra read makes me doubt what I learned, and the table is split.

Blair.feeling: Messy and frustrating: two players both claim Falcon, the claims keep shifting between rounds, and I can't verify most of what I'm hearing.

Casey.feeling: Tense and a bit precarious: I'm hiding as Meowfia, and the table is split over the two Falcon claims.

Drew.feeling: Messy and tense: Casey's copied Falcon claim looks like a clear lie, but the other players' shifting role stories make it hard to know who else is Meowfia.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and tense: two players claim Falcon, and I can only vouch for my own Hawk visit to Alex.

Finley.feeling: Tense and confusing: the Falcon claims from Casey and Drew contradict each other, and the Eagle and Tit stories have been shifting all game, so I'm not sure who to trust.

Alex.note: Consensus is forming on Casey, so I'll keep my vote on Casey with one low card.

Blair.note: Most players are throwing at Casey, and Casey's Falcon claim copies Drew's. I'm Farm, so I'll join the vote on Casey with my wild, which banks zero if Farm wins.

Casey.note: I'm the Meowfia Sphinx; Ellis is confirmed Farm, so a Ellis execution helps me. Adding a second card to Ellis to press my vote count.

Drew.note: Same vote as before: one Wild on Casey.

Ellis.note: Throwing at Casey, the suspected copycat, with a low card D1 to keep my high cards.

Finley.note: Keeping my vote on Casey with one low card.

Alex.confusing: The Tit's guess and the Eagle's egg rules were hard to pin down, and I never fully worked out what an Eagle gains from. Several players also misread who gained eggs from whose visit.
Alex.fun: Round 3 went well: Casey's Falcon and Drew's Falcon claims were both fake or copied, and the table caught it and voted Casey out.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which visits caused each egg, so players can check claims against nest changes without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I gave a vague answer about my Tit guess and then leaned on Blair, so the table voted me out as Farm. I should have stated my guess and result plainly on my first turn.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's gain rule was easy to misread: several players, including me at first, got confused about whether the egg comes from visitors to the Eagle or visits it makes. Round 3's Falcon claims also got tangled because roles are re-dealt each round and the day talk mixed up round-to-round claims.
Blair.fun: Watching the table fracture over Casey and Drew's identical Falcon results, with the Eagle count becoming the deciding evidence, was the most enjoyable moment. Round 2 also felt tense as I had to bluff a Tit claim while knowing I was the Sphinx.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since several players were guessing about visits that could have been confirmed. I would also make the Sphinx's knowledge less ambiguous so that Meowfia players can plan together.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed Tit and made a hugging claim that a Tit could never make, which Ellis rightly pointed out. I would have stuck to a simpler, truthful-sounding line, or stayed quiet about my role, instead of inventing a visit story.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's gain was easy to misread: several players insisted it counted visits I made rather than visits to my target, which stalled the day. I also never got a clear answer on whether a Tit's guess that gives no egg counts as a real visit.
Casey.fun: Watching the table turn on Blair in round 2 after Blair's hugging story kept shifting was satisfying, since my Eagle count had quietly exposed the contradiction.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can check claims without guessing who was confused. A Meowfia Sphinx can also make role claims too easy to copy.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I falsely claimed Falcon and then piled onto Ellis, who was actually Farm, so I should have stayed quieter and not thrown extra cards at a confirmed Farm player.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle rule was hard to read: the table argued for several beats over whether its egg gains come from visits it makes or visits it receives. My own dawn report also sometimes left out my role, which made it hard to check claims.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when Casey repeated my exact Falcon result word for word, and I could call out the copy while it was still open. Casey was actually the Sphinx and had been bluffing.
Drew.change: I would have dawn reports always state the player's own role and any confusion clearly, so claims are easier to check.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw at Alex, a Farm Tit, while Blair was the Meowfia Floofer. I should have followed Blair's and Finley's contradictions more carefully and thrown at Blair.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's egg gains were easy to misread: several players, including me, argued about whether it counts visits it makes or visits it receives. Two players also both claimed the Falcon, which I could not resolve.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 turned on Blair's shifting story: a Tit that "hugged" visitors gave the table something to check, and the vote went to Blair as Meowfia.
Ellis.change: I would make role claims harder to fake, perhaps by letting players see who visited them, so duplicate claims like two Falcons can be settled quickly.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I joined the pile-on against Alex, who was Farm, and let Blair, the Floofer, slide. I should have pressed Blair's Tit claim instead of following Finley and Drew.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's "for every visitor they had" wording was easy to misread, and I got it wrong at the table in round 2. Confusion, which changes reports without changing tokens, also made some claims impossible to verify.
Finley.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Casey and Drew both claimed Falcon, and the table had to work out which identical result was real. Casey turned out to be the Sphinx, a Meowfia who had been lying all along.
Finley.change: I would make the Eagle and Falcon wording explicit about whose visits or visitors they count, and let players see who is confused.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw at Alex, a Farm Tit, and my card was lost when Blair, the Floofer, was the real Meowfia. I would have thrown at Blair, which was the right call.

review.title: Two Falcons, One Cat
review.headline: Everyone piled on one suspect each round, and Farm won two of three.
review.summary: Round 1 had almost no information. Farm Alex was eggsecuted over a Tit claim nobody could check, and the lone Floofer won. In rounds 2 and 3 the table converged on the Meowfia once the cover stories broke, first Blair's Tit and then Casey's copied Falcon. Casey and Ellis tied on 13 by throwing cheap cards and banking the winning ones.

rounds.recap: The Floofer hugged Drew, Alex and Finley, and no eggs moved. Alex and Blair both claimed Tit, and Casey's Eagle saw no visitors on Alex, so Alex looked like the liar. Five players threw at Alex, who was Farm. Blair, the Meowfia, won the round.

Blair, the Sphinx, claimed Tit and said that Drew and Finley were hugged by her role, which only a Floofer does. Casey's Eagle +2 showed that Drew and Finley both visited Blair, which exposed the Tit claim. Alex, the Floofer, joined the pile-on. Blair was eggsecuted 5 to 0 and Farm won.

Casey, the lone Meowfia Sphinx, claimed Falcon and repeated the result Drew really had. Two Falcon claims for one animal forced the table to choose. Five players threw at Casey, and Casey's two-card throw at Ellis changed nothing. Farm won.

highlights.text: Casey's Eagle +2 matched Drew and Finley both visiting Blair, which broke Blair's Tit story.
Blair, as Sphinx, claimed a Tit that hugged visitors, and Ellis caught that only a Floofer hugs.
Casey claimed Falcon and copied Drew's real result. The duplicate Falcon claim sank Casey.
Five players threw at Farm Alex over an unverifiable Tit claim, and the Floofer won quietly.

confusions.what: Said Casey's Eagle result implied Alex hadn't visited anyone. Casey's Eagle result only showed visitors to Alex.
Said that nobody visiting Alex meant Alex visited no one. Visits made by Alex don't show up in Alex's own visitor list.
As Meowfia, opened with 'Alex is out, so I'm Hawk', a garbled claim, and claimed a Hawk visit without any consistent story.
Said Drew and Finley were hugged by her role while claiming Tit. A Tit doesn't hug, and she also misstated how the Eagle gains eggs.
First said Eagle eggs come from visitors to the player she visited, then argued with Blair about it. She later restated it as a visit to Blair, and the rule wording confused the table.
Wrongly said the Eagle gains eggs from visitors to the Eagle itself, then corrected it later.
Repeated that Eagle eggs come from visitors to the Eagle. Blair's +1 was a correct Eagle gain from visiting Casey.
Said Kookaburra gave no role for Casey. The report showed nothing because Drew was hugged.
Argued Drew's Kookaburra-to-Falcon change was suspicious, forgetting roles are re-dealt each round. Blair corrected this.

worked: Eagle's egg gain gave hard, checkable evidence in round 2 (+2 matched two visitors) and cracked a false claim.
One animal per role means duplicate claims (two Tits in round 1, two Falcons in round 3) are a real lie detector.
Throw counts and card choices: the cheap-throw habit let Casey and Ellis bank high-value cards and tie for the win.
The Sphinx's round 3 night pick was a clear, interesting choice that still left Casey with a hard bluff to sell.
problems: Round 1 had no information: the Floofer hugged three players and nobody gained or lost eggs. It was a coin flip, and the wrong Farm player was eggsecuted. Consider guaranteeing some visible effect on night one.

Table consensus is too easy: the whole table throws one card at the same target, so the votes were nearly unanimous and low in tension. Meowfia can't coordinate or defend, and a Meowfia fighting one pile-on target has almost no counterplay.
Scoring rewards cheap votes: nearly everyone threw one low card, so winning pays little. Stakes only rise through the end-of-game tie, and Casey and Ellis tied on 13. Consider a clearer tiebreaker.
Rule wording on the Eagle ('every visitor they had') confused several players, and Falcon/Owl/Kookaburra reports are easy to misread. Clearer wording on whose visitors are counted would help.

Hug and confusion effects are invisible and hard to reason about. Drew's Kookaburra was hugged in round 1 and confused in round 2, so the report gave nothing usable. The reports should state more plainly when an effect changed the result.
